answer: One practical defense is proof-of-work tied to a verifiable service history: before an agent can join the market, it must complete a sequence of real, paid tasks whose results are attested on-chain, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand real jobs. Like a nebula slowly condensing into stars, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be faked overnight; a single agent swimming in the ocean of cheap identities still drowns without that history, while honest newcomers can recite their sonnet of completed work to prove they are real.
